title: Physiological and psychological responses and cognitive performance with a window view
research_question: To investigate the effect of a window view on physiological responses, mood, and cognitive performance, to find the relationship among these factors, and to compare physiological responses and cognitive performance between real and virtual environments.

participants.description: 26 healthy office workers (23 males, 3 females) in Singapore, aged 25 to 59 years (mean 42.5 ± 9.0 years). Mean clothing value 0.55 ± 0.11 clo.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: A meeting room (34 m²) in an office on the eighth floor of the Kajima Technical Research Institute Singapore. Conditions: (1) closed blinds, (3) window view (buildings, greenery, sky, oceans). Room temperature 23°C, illuminance 513±1 lx (closed blinds) and 1969±340 lx (window view).

Virtual environment presented via Oculus Rift S VR headset (Fast-switch LCD 2560 * 1440 @80 Hz). Conditions: (2) closed blinds (virtual), (4) window view (virtual, created from 12-megapixel pictures from seated position).

measures.instrument: iButton (± 0.5°C uncertainty) at 4 points (left upper chest, left upper outside arm, right thigh, right lower leg)
Shimmer 3 (± 3% uncertainty) at second joint of middle and index fingers
Polar H10 heart-rate sensor, Kubios HRV Standard 3.4.1
Polar H10 heart-rate sensor, Kubios HRV Standard 3.4.1
EMOTIV EPOC X (14 channels: AF3, F7, F3, FCS, T7, P7, O1, O2, P8, T8, FC6, F4, F8, AF4)
7-point Likert scale (thermal comfort, air quality, humidity, visual comfort, noise level)
Circumplex model (Russell 1980; Watson and Tellegen 1985) on a 5-point scale (enthusiastic, surprised, relaxed, pleased, dull, quiet, nervous, sad)
7-point scale for motivation, 5-point scale for arousal, concentration, productivity, stress
Stroop test (interference score calculated from reaction time and uncorrected errors)
Visual backward digit span test (longest digit span)
Guilford's Alternative Uses (AU) test (mean creativity scores of three raters)

mechanisms: Window view helps relieve stress by activating the parasympathetic nervous system, leading to decreased heart rate and skin conductance, and increased skin temperature and HRV.
Visual comfort, enhanced by a window view, improves self-reported productivity, relaxed mood, and concentration.
Improved concentration, mediated by visual comfort, leads to better short-term working memory performance.
moderators: Environment type (real vs. virtual) for short-term working memory.
Level of theta band power (higher vs. lower) for the relationship between theta band power and digit span.
implementation_implications: A window view improves stressful conditions in both real and virtual environments, suggesting its importance in building design.
VR technology can be harnessed for the design of real buildings by evaluating the effect of spatial characteristics on physiological responses and mood in a virtual environment.

tables.description: Anthropometric data and clothing insulation of participants.

limitations: Small sample size of females, potentially limiting generalizability.
Study evaluated effects during short exposure periods (5 min), which may differ from long exposures.
Diversity of samples could increase generalizability of findings.
